text.p: Italian sprint star Mario Cipollini won his second stage in as many days in the Tour of the Mediterranean cycle race on Thursday but could not stop Frenchman Emmanuel Magnien from capturing the race lead.
Cipollini, who had claimed Wednesday's opening stage, won a mass sprint to take the first of the second day's two stages, over 72 km from Arles to Rognac.
But an impressive win by the Festina team in Thursday's second stage, a 19-km team time trial from Berre-L'Etang to Velaux, allowed Magnien to take the overall lead.
Frenchmen Richard Virenque and Didier Rous, both team mates of Magnien in the Festina stable, are second and third respectively in the same time as the leader.
